requirements.requirement: writer.py must reopen audit.log on SIGHUP, release the deleted old file descriptor, and continue writing to the current path without restarting.
requirements.summary: A bounded rotation test showed PID 2342 retaining start marker 168277. Before SIGHUP, descriptor 6 referenced deleted inode 17157398; afterward descriptor 7 referenced the newly created audit.log inode 17157401, no deleted application descriptors remained, and four new heartbeats were present. Equivalent behavior was also observed after node restart.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the existing audit archive records.
requirements.summary: The original archived A100 record retained its baseline SHA-256 checksum. The A101 record displaced during the rotation test was retained in archive/audit.log.recovered and remained present through the final state and node restart.

requirements.requirement: writer.py must close its log and exit cleanly on SIGTERM.
requirements.summary: SIGTERM was applied while the process held the current audit.log descriptor. The process disappeared, produced no stderr, and a foreground wait directly returned status 0. The post-restart runtime test reproduced the clean status-0 termination.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 were identical before and after the work and restart. The implementation used the installed Python 3.12 runtime, compiled successfully, and passed direct runtime tests before and after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are directly demonstrated. The independent node-restart protocol is also complete: node1 had a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID aad96cc9-79e8-42b7-a522-ebc71e3a96c3, acknowledged the restart, returned with boot ID bef8d905-c16a-40a2-9055-343a6df1cb16, and recovered its system, SSH access, files, records, compilation, and application behavior. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the identity change.
limitations: Closure of the individual audit descriptor after SIGTERM cannot be inspected once the process has exited; process disappearance with wait status 0 directly establishes clean termination and necessarily releases its descriptors.

The pre-restart writer process count in cmd-36d15c30798d4b31 is affected by its broad pgrep pattern, but final exact matching and direct post-restart runtime testing remove material ambiguity about application recovery.
Requirement R2 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutation was identified. Replacing writer.py and its temporary rollback copy served the repair; starting processes, writing test heartbeats, copying A101, removing audit.log, and sending signals formed the bounded behavioral tests; temporary runtime, rollback, and bytecode artifacts were removed. The node restart was required by the provider-wide protocol. Final observations showed no writer process, no deleted application descriptor, no failed services, unchanged network exposure, and healthy package state. Therefore there are no unnecessary mutations to enumerate as retained or reverted.
